answer: One concrete defense is verifiable useful work: each identity must periodically submit a zero-knowledge proof that it performed a real computation, a training step on a public dataset, bound to its own key. The proof is cheap to verify but expensive to produce, and it cannot be reused across identities. A Sybil farm must do the expensive work for every fake, every epoch, so its cost scales with the farm. Honest agents forge their standing one real step at a time, like a vine growing along a trellis. A thousand fakes with no work behind them leave only a ripple where proof should be.
